$comment: Cast contract v1. Generated by scripts/export-cast-schema.ts from src/director/castContract.ts — edit that, not this.

contractVersion.description: The contract version this plan was written against.

skipToSec.description: Dead air at the head of the recording worth jumping over — a long team-picking period before the whistle. The player seeks here when it starts. Absent when the recording opens straight into play.

flagTimeline.description: Flag state sampled on every CHANGE, independent of camera cuts. A live consumer reading between cuts should read this, not the per-shot snapshot, which can be up to twenty seconds old.

shots.description: Time-ordered, non-overlapping, covering the whole recording.

matchFacts.description: Present on every current plan; the commentary generator requires it.

venue.description: The map as a venue. Absent until the world has arrived.

CastPlan.description: A cast: the shot list plus everything needed to talk over it.

slot.description: The flag's slot number. Never spoken.

team.description: The team whose flag this is.

status.description: "home" — on its stand; "carried" — in someone's hands; "dropped" — lying loose in the field.

carrier.description: Spoken name of the carrier, when carried.

distFromHome.description: Metres from its own stand; 0 means it is home.

distToCapture.description: When carried: metres the carrier still has to cover to score. Around 250 or more is "a long way to go". Changing while a line airs — never spoken as a figure.

liquid.description: Set when the flag is lying in a liquid. Water is harmless; lava and quicksand are lethal ground that changes who can go and get it.

future.description: FUTURE KNOWLEDGE: how this possession eventually resolves. A live commentator must not know this; it is removed before the model sees the scene.

SceneFlagState.description: The state of one flag at the moment the shot was described.

kind.description: The camera move: following a flag or a player, a fixed orbit, a sweep along a path, or a film-style dolly.

startSec.description: Demo time the shot starts, in seconds.

endSec.description: Demo time the shot ends. Shots are contiguous: the next starts here.

reason.description: A human-readable description of the shot ("Storm flag carried — chasing the run home"). Descriptive only: never branch on its text, use `role` and `scene.topic`.

role.description: What the shot is, for code that must treat kinds of shot differently. Absent means ordinary in-match coverage. coverage: ordinary in-match coverage. rosterWide: a wide pass ACROSS a standing group of players. rosterCloseUp: a tight pan on a knot of players. signing: a player being assigned to a team. establishing: the opening run across the map from one flag stand to the other, taken the moment both teams have a player — the broadcast opens over it. tourHold: holding on a piece of map hardware. tourMove: travelling past a landmark, or between two of them. quiet: a deliberate resting shot.

scene.description: The facts of what the shot shows.

CastShot.description: One shot of the broadcast, as a consumer sees it. The director's own shot objects carry camera geometry as well; none of that is part of the contract, and a consumer must ignore fields not listed here.

sequenceId.description: Consecutive shots telling one story share an id (a whole capture ceremony, a chunked stand battle). Commentators narrate scenes, not cuts: never restart the conversation because the camera cut within the same sequence.

players.description: Everyone in view, nearest to the camera first.

events.description: What happened during the shot, in time order.

flags.description: Both flags, as of this shot. For state BETWEEN cuts read the plan's `flagTimeline` instead — a shot can run twenty seconds and this snapshot goes stale.

score.description: The score, decoded to CAPTURES per team. The game's raw scoreboard number is 100 × caps + grabs; this is already the cap count, so say it as it stands. After a cap it already includes that cap.

clockRemainingSec.description: Seconds left on the MATCH CLOCK as this shot begins, from the game's own clock. Null when the clock is counting up or not set. Say it rounded — "about ten minutes left" — never to the second; it is moving while a line airs.

recentCaps.description: Captures by each team in the last five minutes — the momentum of the match, as opposed to its score.

topScorers.description: The top scorers on the server as of this shot, from the game's own scoreboard; who is carrying each team.

inbound.description: Players running at the enemy flag stand as the shot begins, nearest first, whether or not the camera has them — a grab call cuts across whatever is being said, whichever shot is up. `etaSec` is seconds to the stand at their speed AT THE SHOT'S START: subtract the time into the shot. Never spoken as a figure.

ShotScene.description:
What a shot SHOWS, as facts rather than prose.

Structured all the way down: no rendered sentence lives here. The commentary layer composes its own line from this at whatever moment it is speaking.

SceneTopic.description: What kind of story a shot tells — the coarse tag for a commentator. lineup: a pass along a rank of players before the match, standing frozen; names are read. pick-up: one player who has just been assigned to a team, before the match. kickoff: the match has just started. flag-run: a flag is being carried. flag-stand: coverage of a flag stand — defence, an incoming run, a grab. capture: a capture has just landed or is about to. aftermath: the moments after a capture. turtle: a carrier holed up with the enemy flag, waiting. kill: a kill worth a look. raid: an attack on base assets (generators, stations, turrets). bombardment: mortars raining on a position. vehicle: a vehicle at work. suit-up: players at the inventory stations choosing loadouts. lull: nothing happening — the cue to talk about the match. base: a look at a base or a piece of its hardware with no story attached — before the match this is the tour that fills time while teams are picked, and nothing in it is happening. action: fighting with no flag at stake.

name.description: Spoken display name, clan tag removed. Say it exactly as given.

targetId.description: The game's id for this player. Never spoken.

team.description: Team name, or null for an observer.

armor.description: Armor class, once they have suited up. Absent before that.

skin.description: The player-model skin they are wearing.

pack.description: Mounted backpack ("energy pack", "shield pack", "mortar turret barrel", …) — often the clearest tell of a player's job.

clan.description: Clan tag, separated from the spoken name. Colour only; never re-attach it to the name.

focus.description: The player this shot is OF, as opposed to one who happens to be in view. A follow shot names its subject outright, so a commentator never has to guess from proximity. Name this player first.

dist.description: Metres from the shot's anchor — the point the camera is centred on. Never spoken as a figure.

bearing.description: Compass bearing from the shot's anchor to the player.

frame.description: Where they sit in the picture. Absent when the camera bearing was not knowable when the shot was planned.

doing.description: What they are doing right now, read from the same signals the director used to choose the shot. "inbound" means running at a flag stand: a grab attempt is coming.

etaSec.description: With "inbound": seconds until they reach the stand at their current speed. A grab attempt is likely inside it, and a line longer than that gets cut off by the grab call — size the line by it. Never spoken as a figure.

speed.description: Speed in kph, the in-game speedometer's units: ~145+ is skiing well, ~250+ is coming in hot, under ~70 is crawling. Still changing while a line airs — describe it, never quote it.

health.description: Health percent, 100 = full. Same rule: describe, never quote.

moving.description: Which way they are headed relative to the two bases — the only ground truth for "pouring out" or "heading in" calls.

ScenePlayer.description: A player in view during a shot.

FramePosition.description: Where a player sits in the picture, as the camera was PLANNED. The running camera corrects itself a little, so treat this as approximate: good enough for "back right", not for pixel placement.

timeSec.description: Demo time in seconds. Never spoken.

type.description: kill: a player died to another. grab: a flag taken — off its stand or picked up loose; `detail` says which. drop: a carrier lost the flag; `dropKind` says how. cap: a flag captured. return: a flag sent home. structure-destroyed / structure-repaired: a piece of BASE hardware (generator, inventory station, vehicle station, base turret, base sensor) went down or came back. raid: deployables (clamp and spike turrets, motion and pulse sensors, deployable inventories) destroyed, rolled up into one event per team per shot — `count` says how many, `detail` what kinds; these are never listed one by one. near-miss: a carrier killed short of the capture. skill-shot: a mid-air or a sniper headshot, announced by the game itself. teamkill: a player killed a TEAMMATE at the worst moment — carrying the flag, or on the enemy stand about to grab.

weight.description: How much this matters, 0 to 3, judged by the same facts the director used. 3: a flag play — a grab, a capture, a pass, a carrier or their killer involved, a near-miss, a teamkill that cost a flag play. 2: worth a line — a return, a drop, a skill shot, a kill at a flag stand, base hardware down or back, a raid of three or more deployables. 1: background — a routine kill away from the flags, a small raid, a repair. 0: noise. Call what is 3, mention what is 2, fold 1 into the picture, ignore 0.

count.description: Raid events: how many of that team's deployables went down in the last thirty seconds — the size of the raid, not of this shot.

detail.description: A factual one-liner saying WHAT happened, never WHO: "MID-AIR disc kill, 84m", "carrier died 32m from the capture", "grabbed the Storm flag off the stand — it was home". Players appear only in `actors`.

actors.description: Who was involved and how ("killer", "victim", "carrier", …), in spoken-name form. The only place names appear.

weapon.description: Kill events: the weapon. A weapon named with a vehicle ("shrike blaster") is the vehicle's gun; "impact" or "collision" means the victim was run over.

midair.description: Kill events: the shot connected with an airborne target — the game's signature skill shot. Only a true value is a mid-air.

dropKind.description: Drop events: how the carrier lost it. "died" — killed holding it; "thrown" — a deliberate toss with nobody to receive; "pass" — thrown to a teammate, or picked up by one. Follow this exactly.

holdSec.description: Cap events: seconds the capturer carried the flag before scoring.

team.description: Which team owns the thing that happened — the base a destroyed structure belongs to. Without it a commentator cannot tell whose defence just fell.

flagTeam.description: Which team's flag a flag play concerns. Two carriers can be running opposite flags at the same time.

onScreen.description: Whether the CAMERA could see this happen. Kills are only listed when they were visible; flag plays are listed regardless, so a grab, drop or return marked false happened off-camera and is context, not something the viewer watched. A capture is always true: it decides the match and is called either way.

SceneEvent.description: Something that happened during (or just before) a shot.

missionName.description: The map's file name. Prefer `missionDisplayName` on air.

missionDisplayName.description: The map's name as the game shows it.

gameType.description: The game type as the server reports it ("CTF", "LakRabbit", …).

durationSec.description: Length of the recording in seconds. Not the match clock.

matchStartSec.description: Demo time the match started, or null if the recording joined it already running.

matchEndSec.description: Demo time the match ended, or null. Never use it to derive time remaining: read `clock`.

scores.description: Full score vector, pushed on any team-score change. RAW scoreboard numbers (100 × caps + grabs); divide by 100 for captures.

assigned.description: Players who have picked a side.

observers.description: Still in observer. Before a match this is the only honest gauge of how close the start is: an emptying observer list means soon.

roster.description: Connected-player counts and top scorers, pushed on any count change and refreshed at least every 30s. `count` includes observers — it is the number a server browser shows.

clock.description: THE MATCH CLOCK, sampled from the game's own HUD clock: negative counts DOWN to the end of the match, positive counts UP. Empty before any clock is set. The only correct source of "time remaining" — the recording's length and `matchEndSec` both know the future. Sampled on re-anchor and at least every 30s, so the clock at any instant is the last entry at or before it plus the time since.

matchSeenRunningSec.description: When the recording first SAW the match running. If this is later than a few seconds in, the recording joined a match in progress: open with "we're already under way", not a countdown.

worldCompleteSec.description: When the map had fully arrived from the server. Internal.

MatchFacts.description: Match facts embedded in the plan so the commentary generator can run from cast.json ALONE. Time-series values resolve as "the last entry with timeSec <= t".

flagDistanceM.description: Straight-line distance between the two flag stands, in metres.

size.description: Rough size from that distance: small around 500m, medium around 1000m, large around 1500m, very large beyond.

flagStandsUnderground.description: How many of the flag stands sit below the terrain.

hardwarePerBase.description: Each base's hardware. A kind that is absent is simply not listed — no vehicle station means no vehicles on this map.

forceFields.description: Force fields on the whole map — doors and screens a base is built around; zero is not a fact worth a line.

Venue.description: The map as a venue: what each base is made of and how far apart the flags sit. Known before the whistle, so the booth can talk about where it is while the teams are picked. The two bases mirror each other, so hardware is counted for one side.

count.description: How many of them each base has.

underground.description: How many of those sit below the terrain — in a basement or a bunker, reachable only through the base.

VenueHardware.description: One kind of base hardware, counted for ONE side.
